product_family: Anki is a free, open-source spaced-repetition flashcard application with AnkiWeb, a free companion synchronization service. Available on desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux) and mobile (AnkiMobile for iOS, AnkiDroid for Android).

certifications.proof_quote: no public evidence of SOC 2 certification found on AnkiWeb or vendor domains

certifications.proof_quote: no public evidence of ISO 27001 certification found on AnkiWeb or vendor domains

certifications.name: GDPR Compliance Certification
certifications.proof_quote: Privacy policy describes GDPR-compliant data handling practices but no formal GDPR certification or compliance badge mentioned; GDPR is a regulation, not a certification

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: no public evidence of HIPAA compliance; AnkiWeb is a learning tool, not a healthcare/medical records system

privacy.ai_training_note: Anki is a spaced-repetition flashcard learning tool, not a generative AI system. It does not use customer flashcard data to train AI models. Third-party add-ons may integrate with external AI services (e.g., ChatGPT-powered card generators), but AnkiWeb core service does not train on customer data.
privacy.data_region: EU and USA data centers; portions cached via CDN globally

security.name: Encryption in Transit
security.value: HTTPS/TLS for all data synchronization between Anki clients and AnkiWeb

security.name: Encryption at Rest
security.value: No public documentation on encryption at rest for stored flashcards on AnkiWeb servers

security.name: Access Logs Retention
security.value: Access logs retained for 1 month for security and diagnostics, then automatically deleted

security.name: Password Security
security.value: Account security depends on user password strength; AnkiWeb recommends not reusing passwords across sites

security.name: JavaScript Sandboxing
security.value: Limited interface between card JavaScript and Anki internals; arbitrary code execution outside webview unlikely. AnkiWeb uses separate ankiuser.net domain to isolate card content from main site endpoints

security.name: Data Privacy Default
security.value: Flashcards and media are private by default; only shared if user explicitly enables sharing

security.name: Data Retention Policy
security.value: Accounts inactive for 6+ months are marked for deletion; user receives email notification with 30-day grace period to reactivate

security.name: Vulnerability Disclosure Program
security.value: No bug bounty program. Security issues can be reported privately via GitHub security advisory or private message to support

products.name: Anki Desktop
products.data_scope: Offline desktop application; optionally syncs to AnkiWeb for multi-device access
products.notes: Open-source (GitHub: ankitects/anki); free desktop application for Windows, macOS, Linux; handles multimedia (images, audio, video, LaTeX). Can be self-hosted via anki-sync-server (AGPLv3).

products.name: AnkiWeb
products.data_scope: Free online synchronization service for flashcards; optional web-based review interface at ankiweb.net
products.notes: Proprietary (not open-source); free service with no premium tier; hosted on EU and USA data centers with CDN caching. Supports 6-month inactivity cleanup to manage costs.

products.name: AnkiMobile (iOS)
products.data_scope: Official iOS app; syncs with AnkiWeb or self-hosted sync server
products.notes: Paid app ($24.99 USD); revenue funds Anki development; full feature parity with desktop Anki

products.name: AnkiDroid (Android)
products.data_scope: Free and open-source Android app; syncs with AnkiWeb or self-hosted sync server
products.notes: Community-maintained open-source project; available on F-Droid and Google Play; free to use

compare.pricing_model: Freemium: Core Anki and AnkiWeb are free; AnkiMobile (iOS) is paid (~$24.99 USD); AnkiDroid is free open-source
compare.data_residency: AnkiWeb uses EU and USA data centers; users can self-host via anki-sync-server for full control

flags: AnkiWeb is a free, community-driven service with no SOC 2, ISO 27001, or other formal compliance certifications. This is typical for learning tools but limits enterprise adoption.

No public Data Processing Agreement is documented. AnkiWeb's privacy policy addresses GDPR-compliant processing but lacks a formal DPA, which vendors processing EU resident data under GDPR are typically expected to provide.
AnkiWeb's privacy policy confirms HTTPS for data in transit but does not publicly document encryption at rest for stored flashcards.

Researchers documented zero-day remote code execution vulnerabilities exploiting JavaScript in shared decks in 2024. However, there are no documented real-world exploits in Anki's 16-year history, and the desktop app includes mitigations such as domain separation and a limited JavaScript interface.
There is no formal bug bounty program; security reports are accepted only via private channels. This is typical for smaller projects but limits researcher incentives for responsible disclosure.
AnkiWeb is free and may terminate or delete inactive accounts after 6 months. Users should understand service continuity is not guaranteed and should maintain local backups.

AnkiWeb has no dedicated trust center or security documentation portal, unlike many enterprise SaaS vendors. Security information is scattered across the privacy policy, GitHub SECURITY.md, and community forums.
